subject: Dividing counts in facetted barplot to obtain ratio

messages.author: e312c238d72cc18e
messages.subject: Dividing counts in facetted barplot to obtain ratio
parts:
Dear ggplot2 Group members,

I have created the following plot (attached) using the data set AreaTidal2003.csv also attached. Using the following code, where Release_Area and Model are factors:

p1<-qplot(Depth, data=AreaTidal2003,binwidth=10, origin=0,xlim=c(0,150),ylab="Larval Count")+ scale_x_continuous(breaks = breaks, labels=breaks)+facet_grid(Release_Area~Model)

This is fine, however, the raw counts now need to be divided by the original number of particles released. In RA1 35 particles were released every 5 days 7 times, 56 in RA2 also 7 times and 40 in RA3 7 times. So the total number of particles released from each RA is 245 (RA1), 392 in RA2 and 280 in RA3. Is it possible to do this to the count that is generated by qplot, so that all the counts in RA1 are divided by 245, those in RA2 by 392 and those in RA3 by 280?

Thank you!

If I understand the question here is  brute force approach that does it since Releas_Area is already sorted.

ra1  <-  subset (AreaTidal2003$Depth , AreaTidal2003$Release_Area == "RA1")
ra2  <-  subset (AreaTidal2003$Depth , AreaTidal2003$Release_Area == "RA2")
ra3  <-  subset (AreaTidal2003$Depth , AreaTidal2003$Release_Area == "RA3")
ra1  <-  ra1/245
ra2  <-  ra2/392
ra3  <-  ra3/280
  ratio_depth  <-  c(ra1,ra2, ra3)
 
newareatial  <-  data.frame(AreaTidal2003, ratio_depth)

then just do a qplot using ratio_depth in the new data.frame

On Fri, Mar 15, 2013 at 8:18 AM, flatfish <mzo...@hotmail.com> wrote:
> Dear ggplot2 Group members,
>
> I have created the following plot (attached) using the data set
> AreaTidal2003.csv also attached. Using the following code, where
> Release_Area and Model are factors:
>
> p1<-qplot(Depth, data=AreaTidal2003,binwidth=10,
> origin=0,xlim=c(0,150),ylab="Larval Count")+ scale_x_continuous(breaks =
> breaks, labels=breaks)+facet_grid(Release_Area~Model)

This doesn't work in relation to your posted graph since you didn't
specify the order of the Model levels and didn't specify the breaks,
but it was easy enough to fix since you provided a reference graphic,
so thanks.

>
> This is fine, however, the raw counts now need to be divided by the original
> number of particles released. In RA1 35 particles were released every 5 days
> 7 times, 56 in RA2 also 7 times and 40 in RA3 7 times. So the total number
> of particles released from each RA is 245 (RA1), 392 in RA2 and 280 in RA3.
> Is it possible to do this to the count that is generated by qplot, so that
> all the counts in RA1 are divided by 245, those in RA2 by 392 and those in
> RA3 by 280?

There are a couple of ways I guess you could do this. One would be to
create the bins and counts by Release_Area x Mode combination, which
you could do externally, e.g., via the ddply() function in the plyr
package in conjunction with the count() function and either cut() or
findInterval() to produce the necessary bins, after which you could
divide the counts by the number of particles. The resulting data could
then be passed into ggplot2.

Another approach is to use the data generated by ggplot2 when
constructing the faceted graphic, performing some surgery on it and
regraphing. This is the approach taken here.

# Step 0: reorder the factor levels in Model to coordinate with your
posted graphic
AreaTidal2003$Model <- factor(AreaTidal2003$Model,
levels = c("PTS", "LGS", "TDS"))

# Reprise your graphic and save it to an object of class gg named r
r <- qplot(Depth, data = AreaTidal2003, binwidth=10, origin=0,
xlim=c(0,150), ylab="Larval Count") +
facet_grid(Release_Area ~ Model)

# Extract the data component of this object, which contains the data used
# to render the graphic saved in r:
rd <- ggplot_build(r)$data[[1]]

# Modify the data object as follows:
# (i) Add the faceting variables Release_Area and Model, which are related
# to the panel number in rd;
# (ii) add a particles variable whose values correspond to Release_Area;
# (iii) divide ymax by particles to get the larval rate.
rd <- mutate(rd, Release_Area = rep(paste0("RA", seq(3)), each = 48),
Model = factor(rep(levels(AreaTidal2003$Model), each = 16),
levels = levels(AreaTidal2003$Model)),
particles = rep(c(245, 392, 280), each = 48),
rate = ymax/particles)

# Redo the plot with rates instead of counts, replacing geom_histogram() with
# geom_segment()
ggplot(rd) +
geom_segment(aes(x = x, xend = x, y = ymin, yend = rate), size = 5) +
facet_grid(Release_Area ~ Model) +
labs(x = "Depth", y = "Larval Rate") +
scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 150), breaks = seq(0, 140, by = 20))

This is rather non-obvious, but when you want to depart from the
standard conventions in a graphics package, additional work is usually
necessary.

HTH,
Dennis
